episode.title: The Great Fire Of London: Fact Or Ancient Propaganda?

synopsis: While traditional accounts of the 1666 Great Fire of London claim only six victims, the true death toll was likely far greater than recorded.
narration: The Great Fire of London in 1666 consumed 13,200 houses. Official records claim only six deaths, a figure historians now widely dispute. The true human cost, likely buried beneath the ashes, was almost certainly far higher.

shots.prompt: Vertical wide shot of smoke-filled London rooftops in 1666, with flames licking from timber buildings. Panic-stricken but resolute citizens, silhouetted against the fiery glow, attempt to salvage belongings. Camera slowly pans across the destructive panorama, emphasizing chaos but avoiding direct suffering.

Close-up on a soot-stained, bewildered older man, his face illuminated by the flickering orange light of the distant blaze. He clutches a small, charred wooden doll, reflecting profound loss and the overwhelming scale of the devastation. Ash gently falls around him.

music: Fast, tense, percussive underscore with a somber, urgent tone, featuring driving strings and deep, echoing drums, building a sense of historical mystery and tragic scale. The music drives without pause, ending abruptly mid-groove for a seamless loop.
